documents.title: Doc 73 - Infringement - Car 27 - Impeding of Car 55
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 27 - Impeding of Car 55

details.fact: Car 27 impeded Car 55 in turn 5
details.infringement: Breach of Article B4.1.1 of the FIA F1 Regulations.
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 27 (Nico Hulkenberg), the driver of Car 55 (Carlos Sainz), team representatives and reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video, team radio, timing and in-car video evidence. Video showed that Car 27 was driving slowly on the racing line on the approach to turn 5. Car 55 arrived from behind on a push lap and had to abandon the lap. That Car 55 was thereby impeded was not in dispute. The issue was whether Car 55 had been ‘unnecessarily’ impeded. The team stated in the hearing that they believed, based on timing information to which they subscribed, sourced from the official timekeeping provider, that Car 55 had already taken the chequered flag and conveyed that information to the driver by radio. Therefore the driver of Car 27 did not expect Car 55 to still be on a push lap when it was closing in. The Stewards acknowledge the fact that the data referenced by the team led the team to reasonably believe that Car 55 had received the chequered flag. Indeed, it was evident from Car 55’s radio messages that its team had formed the same belief relying on the same data. The misunderstanding was revealed to be attributable to the information initially received by the teams not being fully synchronised and only being displayed in a correct manner after a short period of time. However, that post-processing did not occur until Car 55 arrived behind Car 27 depriving the team of any reasonable opportunity to correct the information conveyed to the driver. In the Stewards’ assessment, because the source of the data upon which the team relied was the official timing provider, it was not unreasonable for the team to have relied upon it, even though the team also had available to it the official timing data which conflicted. On the objective facts, the Stewards determined that Car 55 was unnecessarily impeded. However, there were extraordinary mitigating circumstances in this case because the incident was attributable to the team’s reliance on information that was, for a brief period, inconsistent.

documents.title: Doc 62 - Infringement - Car 77 - Causing a Collision with Car 23
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 77 - Causing a Collision with Car 23

details.fact: Car 77 collided with Car 23 in Turn 16
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 d) of the International Sporting Code.
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 5 (Gabriel Bortoleto), the driver of Car 23 (Alexander Albon), the driver of Car 77 (Valtteri Bottas), team representatives and reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video and in-car video evidence. When preparing for the re-start at the end of a Safety Car period, Car 23 collided with the rear of Car 5, and Car 77 collided with the rear of Car 23. The driver of Car 77 said that he had no opportunity to avoid colliding with the rear of Car 23 after Car 23 checked-up after it collided with Car 5. In the Stewards’ assessment both collisions were a consequence of a concertina created by cars ahead travelling at inconsistent speeds in the preparation for the re- start. As Cars 23 and 77 were towards the back of the pack of slow moving cars, the chain reaction effect on them was more pronounced. Nonetheless, the Stewards determined that like the collision between Cars 23 and 5, the collision between Cars 77 and 23 could have been avoided had the driver of Car 77 recognised the risk of a concertina ahead and left more space when following Car 23, particularly having regard to the damp conditions. Had Car 77 not retired from the Sprint as a consequence of the collision, the Stewards would have imposed a 5 second time penalty rather than the usual 10 second time penalty taking into account that, in part at least, a number of cars ahead in the queue had contributed by slowing at inconsistent rates. A 5 second time penalty would not have been converted into a grid penalty and therefore the Stewards determined not to apply a penalty in this case.

documents.title: Doc 59 - Decision - Car 81 - Alleged causing a collision with car 1
documents.subject: Decision - Car 81 - Alleged causing a collision with car 1

details.fact: Car 1 and Car 81 collided at turn 5
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 81 (Oscar Piastri), the driver of Car 1 (Lando Norris), team representative and reviewed video and in-car video evidence. The driver of Car 1 attempted to overtake Car 81 on the inside at Turn 5. A collision occurred at the apex. The driver of Car 81 explained that he had not expected Car 1 to attempt an overtake and, after turning in, noticed Car 1 on the inside and attempted to leave space. The driver of Car 1 said that he saw an opportunity to overtake. He said that the front axle of his car was ahead of the mirror of Car 81 prior to the apex and therefore expected to be left space. As he approached the apex, the space was less than he had anticipated so he had to use the inside kerb and braked and a collision occurred. The Stewards considered that both drivers had contributed to the incident and that neither driver was wholly or predominantly to blame for the collision. Therefore the Stewards determined to take no further action.

documents.title: Doc 56 - Decision - Car 41 - Alleged driving opposite direction
documents.subject: Decision - Car 41 - Alleged driving opposite direction

details.competitor: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls F1 Team
details.fact: The Driver drove in the wrong direction at Turn 5
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article 12.2.1.h of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 41 (Arvid Lindblad), team representative and reviewed video and in-car video evidence. Car 41 spun after the exit of Turn 5 and was facing towards oncoming cars. Car 41 drove in the wrong direction for approximately 100 metres back to Turn 5 and used the run-off area to turn around. The Driver explained that he could not perform a flick turn from the position in which his car was stopped after the spin. Because he was facing the wrong way, he drove back a short distance against oncoming traffic but staying to the edge of the track and away from the racing line. After he was sure the last car had passed, the Driver of Car 41 attempted a flick turn but the car would not rotate. The Driver explained that, knowing that the last car had passed and it would present no danger for him to continue, he drove back to turn 5 where he knew there would be space to turn. Having regard to the difficult position the Driver of Car 41 found himself in, where his car was originally prone and then unable to turn, and given further that there was no oncoming traffic, the Stewards determined that what occurred was not in these circumstances unsafe and therefore took no further action.

documents.title: Doc 54 - Decision - Car 11 - Causing a collision with Car 18
documents.subject: Decision - Car 11 - Causing a collision with Car 18

details.fact: Car 11 collided with Car 18 in Turn 16
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 18 (Lance Stroll), the driver of Car 11 (Sergio Perez), team representatives and reviewed video and in-car video evidence. Car 11 attempted to overtake Car 18 on the inside into Turn 16 and both cars made contact. The Stewards determine that the driver of Car 11 initiated the overtaking attempt in a legitimate way, but then locked up the front right wheel therefore was not able to rotate the car anymore. The Stewards determine the the driver of Car 11 was predominantly at fault, but also take into account the weather conditions and acknowledge the difficulties of controlling the car on the brakes in such circumstances. Therefore a 5 second time penalty is deemed appropriate and would have been applied in-race if that had been possible. As Car 11 was not classified and 5 second time penalties regularly do not convert into grid drops, no penalty is applied in this case.

details.infringement: Breach of Appendix H, Article 2.5.5b of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 3 (Max Verstappen), the driver of Car 44 (Lewis Hamilton), team representatives and reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video, timing, telemetry, team radio and in-car video evidence. As Car 3 was exiting turn 7 on a push lap, a single yellow flag was displayed. Car 44 was ahead of Car 3 and had been warned of Car 3’s approach. The Driver of Car 44 said that after exiting turn 7, he slowed and moved to the right to ensure he was off the racing line. Car 3 overtook Car 44 prior to turn 8 while both cars were still in the yellow flag sector. Car 3 then abandoned the push lap. The Driver of Car 3 explained that he was on throttle exiting turn 7 and then saw the yellow flag and lifted. This was confirmed by telemetry. Within approximately 40 metres of entering the yellow flag sector, the Driver of Car 3 had lifted fully off throttle. The Driver of Car 44 was braking and had reduced speed to less than 60km/h at the point Car 3 overtook. Because Car 3 was on a push lap and was on throttle out of turn 7 and Car 44 had slowed, the speed differential at the point of the overlap was significant despite the fact that the Driver of Car 3 had also started braking. The Stewards were satisfied that the Driver of Car 3 reacted appropriately to the yellow flag by lifting off throttle and reducing speed. The speed of Car 3 at the overtake point was some 70km/h less than Car 3’s speed on another push lap in the same session. The Driver of Car 3 explained that to have avoided the overtake would have required him to have braked very heavily and he considered to have done so would have potentially created an unsafe situation. The Stewards determined that the Driver of Car 3 breached the yellow flag regulation by overtaking Car 44. However, the Stewards were satisfied that the overtake was an unfortunate consequence of the significant closing speed differential and, in these circumstances, determined not to impose a penalty.

details.fact: The following Power Unit elements have been used: 5th Engine (ICE) 5th Turbocharger (TC) 5th Exhaust Set (EXH) 4th MGU-K
details.infringement: Breaches of Articles B8.2.2 (read with B8.2.3) of the FIA F1 Regulations.
details.decision: Drop of 40 grid positions in the next Race in which the driver participates.
details.reason: The penalty is imposed in accordance with Article B8.2.8 of the FIA F1 Regulations. The use of each additional element in this case carries a 10 grid place penalty therefore there is an accumulation of 40 places. Subject to Car 63 being classified in the results of Qualifying, Car 63 will be allocated a grid position in the Race in accordance with Article B2.5.4b.iv of the FIA F1 Regulations.
